content:
Overview:
KARL MAYER is a mechanical engineering company that offers a wide range of products and services of its sector with the focus on textile machinery building. The business activities are concentrated on the fields of warp knitting, technical textiles and warp preparation for weaving. KARL MAYER supports the success of its international customers with products and services that are outstanding in both economic and technical terms, as well as with innovations that move the textile world forward. KARL MAYER has employees all over the world. Thanks to its global organization and its claim to produce in its main markets, the company is always close to its customers and their needs. Today, it has subsidiaries in the USA, India, Italy, Hong Kong, Japan, China, Turkey, India and Switzerland, as well as agencies in all parts of the world. KARL MAYER is a German family-owned company, which has focused on financial independence and economic sustainability since its foundation in 1937. As a permanent, reliable partner with decades of experience and a high level of quality in all areas, it supports the competitiveness of its customers and business partners. title: Karl Mayer celebrates 35 years of EL pattern drive
content: OBERSHAUSEN, Germany – Karl Mayer is marking a milestone this year: on Nov. 30, 1990, the company delivered its first warp knitting machine with electronic guide bar control, the KS 4 EL. The SU drive, first used in Multibar Raschel machines, controlled the shogging movement of the guide bars magneto-mechanically through actuators and a microcomputer. A version of the SU drive with an integrated overlap device, developed in 1985, also allowed tricot machines to eliminate pattern chains and discs, clearing the way for further electronic advancements. To overcome the mechanical limitations of the SU drive on tricot machines, Karl Mayer developed an electrically powered system, breaking new ground in the process. The prototype led to the first electronic guide bar control system, launching a new era. After an upgrade for high-bar models, the first Multibar Raschel machine with electronic control of all guide bars — the TL 66 — debuted in 2002.

title: KARL MAYER (China) celebrates its 30th anniversary
content: On February 6, KARL MAYER (China) celebrated the new year and its 30th anniversary. Employees and the management team at the Changzhou location, as well as representatives from management in Germany, Italy, and Hong Kong, were invited to the festivities. A special highlight was the visit by Lutz Wolf, CEO of KARL MAYER. The establishment of a separate company in China in the mid-1990s was a bold and strategically consistent step. In the early 1980s, KARL MAYER collaborated with the Wujin Textile Machinery Factory in Changzhou for joint production and to promote knitting technology in China. In 1995, the two partners joined forces with NIPPON MAYER to found KARL MAYER WUJIN Textile Machinery Co., Ltd. The joint venture was the first company with foreign roots in the Changzhou Wujin High-tech Zone. The latest milestone in the success story of KARL MAYER’s Chinese location was the opening of a new showroom in October 2024, featuring an exclusive selection of textile highlights, trend themes, and innovative solutions from all business units.
